newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mixed Australian stocks end little changed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mixed Australian stocks end little changed.

text.p: The Australian share market ended the way it started on Thursday, just weaker and narrowly mixed, with a firmer resources sector failing to overcome a Dow-weakened industrials group.
By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.9 points lower at 2,436.3. March share price index futures were down four points at 2,446, a 9.7 point premium to the index.

The market spent most of its day meandering in a five point range with only a late burst of interest in bellwether BHP and National Australia Bank bringing the benchmark indicator back to within a whisker of square.
"Apart from the gold stocks, the resource sector is quite firm. BHP, WMC and Pasminco are leading the way," said Steve Mayne, dealer at Nevitts Ltd.
"Banks are a bit flat and so are golds so it is a bit of a mixed bag."
Mayne was impressed by the performance given continuing weakness in the gold price and a fall on Wall Street.

"It's been a pretty good performance to be only down a couple of points with the gold price so weak and Wall Street down," he said, adding that the market looked comfrotable with its recent higher levels.
"Our market looks pretty strong really, with reasonable volumes behind it."
Smaller companies featured, Dragon Mining seeing active trade again after Wednesday's announcement of a nickel find at its 35 percent-owned Weld Range prospect in Western Australia.
After spiking 30 percent early to reach 21.9 cents, the temptation to cash in quick profits proved too great with sellers emerging to see the stock close at 15.5 cents.
Metals processor Queensland Metals Corporation soared nearly 30 percent after it and Normandy Mining announced the development of the Magmetal magnesium project in Queensland.
Despite profit takers, who knocked it off its early A$1.51 highs, QMC shares closed 17 cents higher at A$1.34 on solid turnover of 2.83 million shares.
"QMC had a big announcement and saw quite a deal of interest. They were one of the big rises today." Mayne said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 10 to nine, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was moderately active with both markets slowing from Wednesday's solid volumes.
Total options traded 32,115 (46,108)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 4,524 (6,501)

In other local markets, Australian bonds retreated to negative territory as some signs of strength in December labour force data dented sentiment. By 4.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.45 percent, compared to 7.41 Wednesday.

The Australian dollar dipped into danger on Thursday after surrendering another support level to fears of a domestic rate cut and an exodus of offshore funds. The loss deepened the technical gloom engulfing the currency and left dealers happy to go short in the belief last week's 5-1/2 month low at US$0.7738 would soon be surpassed. By 4.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7757/62, down from US$0.7777/82 Wednesday.
